system.description: Demesure is a sinful pride that exacts extraordinary, sometimes horrendous costs from its possessor and everyone around him — the most famous example is Childe Roland, who refused to let his men retreat before the Moors rather than appear a coward. The player, with the Storyteller, selects one or more things the character takes great pride in: his clothes, his horsemanship, his prowess in battle. Whenever that pride is insulted or threatened, the character must resist or become obsessed with salvaging his "honor" to the exclusion of all other business, a fixation that can cost him allies, ruin careful plans, or get him and those he cares for killed. Each time he achieves a goal related to the obsession, he may attempt to let it rest for the remainder of the night.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book One: Artisans (Toreador)
